text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia,
situated in the Pacific Ocean. It comprises
four main islands—Honshu, Hokkaido,
Kyushu, and Shikoku—and numerous
smaller islands. Known for its unique
blend of ancient traditions and cutting-
edge technology, Japan has a rich cultural
heritage, including temples, tea ceremonies,
and festivals, alongside being a global
leader in innovation and pop culture.
With a population of approximately 123 million, Japan is the world's fourth-largest economy
by nominal GDP. The country faces demographic challenges including an aging population and
low birth rate. Japanese society is known for its safety, efficiency, and high standard of living.
The official language is Japanese, and the currency is the Japanese Yen (JPY).
Japan's economy is the fourth-largest in
the world by nominal GDP. After decades
of growth, the economy has faced
challenges including deflation, an aging
population, and global economic
fluctuations. The GDP peaked around
2019 and has seen a decline in recent
years due to currency depreciation and
global economic conditions.
• Tokyo: Vibrant capital with modern districts,
historic temples, and world-class dining.
• Kyoto: Ancient capital with over 1,600 temples,
traditional geisha districts, and gardens.
• Osaka: Known for its modern architecture,
nightlife, and hearty street food.
• Hiroshima/Miyajima: Peace Memorial Park
and the iconic floating torii gate.
• Mount Fuji/Hakone: Japan's highest peak
and hot spring resorts with views of Fuji.
• Hokkaido: Northern island famous for natural
beauty, skiing, and fresh seafood.
Source: World Bank, IMF, Statistics Japan (2024 estimates)
